sources.title: InSCIt: Information-Seeking Conversations with Mixed-Initiative Interactions
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 11, pp. 453-468 (presented at ACL 2023)
sources.supports: A dataset of 805 human-human conversations (4.7K user-agent turns) in which users may ask under-specified or unanswerable questions and the Wikipedia-searching agent either answers directly, asks for clarification or provides relevant information; baselines fall well short of humans.
sources.correction: The abstract says 'under-specified or unanswerable' (not 'incomplete'); 'giving relevant information without claiming to resolve the question' is a fair paraphrase of the 'provides relevant information' strategy, not a quoted phrase.

sources.title: Analysing Mixed Initiatives and Search Strategies during Conversational Search
sources.venue: CIKM '21 (30th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management), pp. 16-26
sources.supports: A simulation/model study on 49 TREC Web Track topics finding no dominant combination of initiative (ask first vs after results) and approach (query clarification vs query suggestion); the best choice depends on the relative costs of querying and giving feedback, initial query performance, assessments per query and total gain required.
sources.correction: The compared options are clarifications vs query suggestions and asking before vs after results (not 'asking vs giving information'); evidence is simulation over TREC topics, not a user study.

sources.citedAs: a 2022 study on user experience of the quality and order of clarifying questions
sources.title: Asking Clarifying Questions: To Benefit or to Disturb Users in Web Search?
sources.venue: Information Processing & Management 60(2), article 103176 (online 26 Nov 2022; issue March 2023)
sources.identificationConfidence: high: the only 2022 work found that studies both quality and order ('trajectory') of clarifying questions with effects on satisfaction and behaviour; but the citation is unspecified, so the match is inferred
sources.supports: A user study with 89 participants on web search tasks: the trajectory of clarifying-question quality changes SERP interaction (a preceding low-quality CQ suppresses engagement), follow-up high-quality CQs recover performance and satisfaction, and showing only high-quality CQs gives better gains with less effort, so low-quality CQs disturb users.
sources.correction: Cite as Zou et al., Information Processing & Management 2023 (online 2022); the setting is web search with CQs shown alongside results, not a full conversational dialogue.

sources.title: Table Extraction and Understanding for Scientific and Enterprise Applications
sources.venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment 13(12), pp. 3433-3436 (VLDB 2020 tutorial)
sources.supports: The abstract defines table extraction as identifying border and cell structure and table understanding as linking cells with semantic information inside and outside the table (row/column headers, footnotes, titles, references in surrounding text), and states that cells must be linked to headers, units of measure and in-text references.
sources.correction: It is a 4-page tutorial abstract (a synopsis of existing approaches), not a research paper with new results; cite it for the definitions only.

sources.citedAs: a 2024 survey of document-level information extraction
sources.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Document-Level Information Extraction
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on the Future of Event Detection (FuturED), ACL Anthology, pp. 58-72, Miami
sources.identificationConfidence: medium-high: the 2024 survey whose abstract names coreference and reasoning problems; earlier arXiv version 2309.13249 (2023, 'A Survey of Document-Level Information Extraction')
sources.supports: A review plus error analysis of state-of-the-art document-level IE finding that entity coreference resolution and weak reasoning remain major obstacles, with labeling noise and relation transitivity as further challenges.
sources.correction: The abstract names labeling noise (dataset annotation quality) rather than 'evaluation datasets' in general; it is a workshop paper, not a journal survey.

sources.title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2019), PMLR 97, pp. 2151-2159
sources.supports: Proposes a network with an integrated reject option trained end-to-end for prediction and selection at a target coverage, reporting improved risk-coverage trade-offs over threshold-on-confidence baselines in classification and regression.

sources.title: Resolving Conflicting Evidence in Automated Fact-Checking: A Study on Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
sources.venue: Proceedings of IJCAI-25, AI and Social Good track, pp. 9656-9664
sources.supports: Introduces CONFACT and shows RAG models' reliability drops with conflicting evidence, especially when conflicts stem from differing media-source credibility; adding source-credibility information at retrieval and generation improves conflict resolution.
sources.correction: The setting is automated fact-checking, not general retrieval-augmented question answering.

sources.citedAs: The Illusion of Generalization in Tabular Language Models
sources.title: The Illusion of Generalization in Tabular Language Models
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026), PMLR 306, pp. 36369-36396
sources.supports: Re-evaluates Tabula-8B on the 165 UniPredict datasets: near-zero median gain over majority class on binary/categorical tasks, aggregate scores driven by quartile classification, widespread train-test contamination and task-level leakage, and instruction tuning without tabular data recovering 92.2% of classification performance, so claimed generalisation likely reflects evaluation artefacts.
sources.correction: The re-examined model is Tabula-8B specifically; venue is ICML 2026 (arXiv 2602.04031).
